reviews.title: What we needed was a system.
reviews.body: This is what I wish discharge instructions had been: one house rule, one routine, one card for when it looks wrong.
reviews.name: Nneka

reviews.title: The re-entry protocol saved us.
reviews.body: What I needed was not more information. I needed a default that holds when we are tired — and a way to recover after a bad night without guilt. This gave us both.
reviews.name: Tolu

reviews.title: Finally a system, not just advice.
reviews.body: I can see how the 3-week notice works when life cooperates. Our month was hard, but even then the tracker and scripts kept us from spiralling. With a calmer month it would have been even better.
reviews.name: Hauwa

reviews.title: We stopped arguing about whose turn it is.
reviews.body: We went from Googling at 3am to checking one chart on the fridge. Both adults see it, both follow it. The argument stopped before it started.
reviews.name: Lola

reviews.title: The fairness ledger changed everything.
reviews.body: We spent months negotiating every night and blaming each other. The 3-Week Notice ended the negotiation. It is not magic — some nights are still hard — but nobody has to ask, and that was the whole problem.
reviews.name: Bisi

reviews.title: The scripts did what I could not say.
reviews.body: The 3-Week Notice is practical. It replaces asking with a pre-agreed default. We hit the bad-night protocol twice and having a reset instead of a meltdown — mine — is the part I did not know I needed.
reviews.name: Ezinne

reviews.title: My partner finally understood the load.
reviews.body: My mother-in-law kept wanting to rub things on the stump. The family script let me hold the rule without a fight. That alone was worth it.
